name: Fatpill

card.summary: A looksmaxxing-forum term for the idea that body fat level strongly shapes how attractive someone looks, used to frame leaning out as a major appearance lever.
card.note: Slang term; the community also uses it in mocking ways toward overweight people.

quick.overview:
Fatpill is forum shorthand for the belief that body fat is a central driver of looks. In looksmaxxing circles it is used to explain why some faces and physiques look noticeably sharper after fat loss, and it is the premise behind advice to address leanness before anything else.

The term sits alongside other community 'pills'. Threads using it debate whether leanness really helps, for example weighing a study on weight and sexual activity against the idea that lean men look better. Research on attractiveness separately reports that facial and body fat influence perceived health, youthfulness and jawline definition.
quick.how: In practice the idea is applied by tracking body weight or body fat, dieting and training to lose fat, and comparing before and after photos for jawline, cheekbone and physique definition. Community discussion also covers height and frame, with some users saying leanness works best on tall men.
quick.risks: As a belief it carries no direct physical risk, but crash dieting and extreme leanness pursued for looks carry the usual health costs described in medical literature. The term itself is sometimes used derisively toward larger people in forum threads.

lead: Fatpill is a looksmaxxing-community term for the belief that body fat has an outsized effect on appearance, so that fat loss reveals jaw, cheekbone and physique definition that excess weight hides. It is the 'pill' people take when they conclude that leanness is the main variable in how they look.

Discussion on looksmax.org shows the term contested: one thread asks 'Is the fatpill legit?', citing a study reported by PsyPost that found being overweight linked to more frequent sexual activity in men but less in women, and asks whether leanness is overrated.[1] Replies argue that leanness works best on tall men and that other factors such as class and ethnicity could explain the pattern.[1]

Wider attractiveness research reports that men with less submental fat were viewed as having better jawlines and looking more youthful, and that facial shape cues of body fat influence perceived health.[2]

chain: Facial bone structure and jawline become more visible
Physique looks more defined and healthier
angle.text: Proponents treat fat loss as the most direct lever on both face and body: lower facial fat sharpens the jaw and cheeks, and a lower waist relative to chest and shoulders reads as more attractive. How much weight to lose is debated within the community.

paras: Fatpill refers to a mindset or claim about body fat rather than a product. Forum users invoke it either to say that excess fat explains much of a person's perceived unattractiveness, or to ask whether the importance of leanness is exaggerated.[1]

Attractiveness literature summarized on Wikipedia reports that waist-to-chest ratio was the largest determinant of male attractiveness in one study, that body weight had a stronger effect than waist-to-hip ratio in another, and that ideals vary by culture, for example traditional acceptance of body fat in Samoa.[2] The same source notes that low under-chin fat was associated with better-judged jawlines.[2]

Users weigh leanness against factors such as height, noting that a lean frame can read differently on shorter men.[1] Some replies treat the topic as a debate about whether being lean is truly an advantage with women or only matters in appearance terms.[1]
No studies found. Related research on attractiveness and body composition exists but does not test the forum concept itself.[2]

lore.intro: The term appears in debates over whether leanness or heavier builds are advantageous.[1]

claims.claim: Being lean is the main thing separating average from good-looking
claims.believers: Proponents say fat loss exposes facial structure and improves physique proportions.[1]
claims.experts: Attractiveness research links lower facial fat to better-judged jawlines and perceived health, while ideals vary by culture.[2]

claims.claim: Overweight men do better romantically than lean ones
claims.believers: A forum poster cited a news report of a study finding more sexual activity in overweight men.[1]
claims.experts: Replies in the same thread proposed confounders such as socioeconomic and ethnic differences; no controlled test is cited.[1]
